layout.description: Real run, recorded on Nov 3, 2026 with Claude Code 2.1.309 (model claude-haiku-5-5). A made-up customer list with 40 rows, 9 of them duplicates. Run 1 with a short prompt, run 2 with an exact rule, each twice. Both times 31 customers were left, counted. With the short prompt Claude named its rule itself and flagged one decision to check.
layout.companion_text: Base command per run: claude -p "<Prompt>" --model haiku --output-format stream-json --verbose --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --no-session-persistence --tools Read,Write. Tools Read and Write, --permission-mode acceptEdits; both prompts end with "Reply in English.". Run 2 states the rule in the prompt (same e-mail, ignoring case and spaces at the edges). Paths shortened in the frame (test folder = .). Behaviour can change with version and model. Not an official Anthropic channel.

beats.spoken: 40 customers, some of them duplicates. Does Claude Code clean up the list correctly? I let it run for real and counted.
The test list is made up. Nine rows are duplicates, six of them exactly the same. Three are tricky: Müller with ü and with ue, Office once with a capital letter, and once a space after the e-mail.
Run one only gets the short prompt. No rule for what a duplicate is.
Claude reads the file, thinks briefly and writes the cleaned list. After 18 seconds the answer: 31 customers are left.
I counted: 31 is correct. All nine duplicates are gone, including Mueller, the capital Office and the trailing space.

data.note: Also caught: Mueller, Office, trailing space

beats.spoken: The interesting part is the answer. Claude picked the rule itself: same e-mail, upper or lower case. And it tells you what to check: Mueller and Müller could be two companies.

picks: I treated two rows as duplicates when they had the same email address, ignoring case and stray spaces.
The last one is a judgment call.
If you want matching by name as well as email, "Mueller GmbH" should stay, which would leave 32 customers.

beats.spoken: Run two states the rule explicitly. Result: also 31, the same nine rows removed. Each run ran twice, the same every time.
Here the short prompt was enough. But only the answer shows which rule was used. Read it before you use the list. Follow Promptwerk for real Claude Code runs.

data.statement: Read the answer, not just the number.
